correctness.rationale: For every even n>=6, the fixed locus of each index reflection is a disjoint union of boundary-square mirror circles: its two exceptional index-orbits may vary separately but have nonadjacent supports. Every other orbit is forced to an endpoint sign. Distinct reflection mirrors intersect only at sign vertices because their product is a nonidentity rotation fixing no positive-dimensional cell. Their union is the exact labelled binary sign-word graph; the boundary is its dihedral quotient. The two independently specified exact n=10 computations enumerate all sign-mirror components and all barycentric quotient flags, giving ten boundary circles, chi=-74, a length-15 orientation-reversing dual walk, hence a nonorientable connected surface with 66 crosscaps. Actual executable package checks were rerun and deterministic outputs matched. The all-even theorem rests on geometric proof, not finite sampling. The exact n=10 enumeration is exhaustive, not approximate.

value.rationale: On compact bordered surfaces, Euler characteristic and free fundamental-group rank do not determine homeomorphism type. The existing full-dihedral result expressly leaves even polygon boundary and orientability open. The new all-even exact mirror-graph model is structural and yields an efficient method for actual boundary classification; the first non-power-of-two even width at n=10 has b=10 and an explicit nonorientable N_{66,10} homeomorphism class. This natural transition resolves an otherwise undetermined topological invariant rather than an arbitrary table slice. The proof does not claim an unproved all-width closed formula.
